title: GPT-5.6 sol audit latent batch (7/09–7/10): projected-DD early lock (F2), green crash loop (F3), dead health checks (F4, F6), R2 sync (F8), F10, stale unit (F12), scoring race (F13), F15, R4
tier_reason: no harmful firing is evidenced for any link; tier A by the B -> A rule: unfixed residuals (streak/pick two-file pair under a crash, postponed cached-fallback delivery, manual-run and final-fallback lineup-gate bypasses, F6 fingerprint scope, best-effort churn check) can still change state, delivery or alerting; F3 (liveness), F8/F12 (recoverability), F13 (state) and F2/R4 (delivery) are A-class if they fire

contract.text: Each audited path meets its contract: a normal early lock commits only lineup-confirmed selected slots whose games are still available (F2, R4); a torn state file never yields a crash loop that monitors score healthy (F3); a crashing health check surfaces CRITICAL (F4); realized_calibration evaluates the current regime's last 30 days once 5 bucket picks exist (F6); an interrupted R2 sync leaves the prior manifest restorable (F8); the skip-shadow verdict and its breakeven are reproducible from the repo and valid under nightly re-looks (F10); the repo's tracked units reproduce production (F12); each result changes streak state at most once (F13); and `bts preview` defaults to tomorrow in ET (F15).
contract.source: F2: strategy.should_lock docstring condition 2 at 9643d83; R4: design §10.3 postponed cached-fallback oracle ('no delivery naming a postponed game') + 6d74d39 R4; F3: util.atomic_write_text docstring (audit D1) at a349ac5; F4: health/runner.py _safe_run docstring (audit H3, 0f2bc3c); F6: health/realized_calibration.py module docstring (30-day lookback, minimum bucket count 5); F8: data/sync.py sync_to_r2 docstring 'Writes the manifest last, atomically' at cca6761; F10: docs/audit/2026-06-20-skip-policy-shadow.md (verdict vs the 0.744 breakeven) + audit F10; F12: audit memo raw finding 12 (DR from the tracked unit); F13: design §10.3 scoring crash/restart oracle ('one result affects streak and saver at most once') + ARCHITECTURE.md 'Scoring serialization'; F15: cli.py preview --date help 'Defaults to tomorrow' + the _today_et ET convention

mechanism.text: F2: should_lock rejected only a projected primary and _lock_decision_from_predictions passed only daily.pick, so on a double day a projected double-down rode the primary's confirmation through the normal early lock (the gap rule was built for a single pick racing projected alternatives)

F3: save_state wrote scheduler_state.json with a bare write_text and load_state parsed it with no recovery, while run_day wrote the RUNNING heartbeat and signalled READY/watchdog before loading state; a torn file would crash every start and restart every 30 s with a fresh heartbeat, check_heartbeat scored any fresh 'running' heartbeat healthy, restart_spike ran only at EOD inside the crashing process and the deploy canary checked is-active at +30 s

F4: calibration, projected_lineup, post_failure and disk_fill caught exceptions inside check() and returned [], so an evaluation failure looked healthy and never reached _safe_run's CRITICAL-on-crash conversion (the audit-H3 contract)

F6: realized_calibration.check dropped every pick whose run_time preceded the latest deploy stamp and every deploy (docs, shadow, ops) re-stamped, so the bucket sample could not reach min_bucket_n while deploys were frequent and the check was effectively dead

F8: sync_to_r2 overwrote stable object keys before replacing the manifest, so an interrupted sync left the old manifest pointing at new bytes; sync_from_r2 downloaded into the final path and deleted it on a checksum mismatch; verify_manifest checked only manifest metadata and age

F10: the skip-policy shadow re-tested a fixed-N 95% Wilson interval against the 0.744 breakeven at every nightly rebuild (repeated looks, not time-uniform), and the breakeven's derivation existed only as /tmp/skip_qdelta.py on the box, outside the repo

F12: the tracked scripts/bts-scheduler.service was the stale Pi5 unit (Type=simple, /home/stonehengee paths, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=300) while production ran notify + watchdog with Restart=always/30 s; no dashboard unit was tracked and nothing detected drift, so a rebuild from the repo would install a broken unit

F13: check-results (01:00 cron) and the daemon's result polling (until 05:00) each did load pick -> resolve -> update_streak -> save_pick with no shared lock (only saver state had a flock), and the daemon's cap/unresolved/suspended writers and the 02:00 reconcile_results also wrote unlocked, so an interleave could double-apply or lose a streak update or overwrite a terminal result
F15: bts preview computed its default date as UTC now + 1 day, so a manual run between about 20:00 and 23:59 ET wrote the slate for the day after tomorrow (the 03:00 ET cron was unaffected)

R4: _lock_decision_from_predictions status-filtered contender rows but not the already-selected pick/double-down, so a selected game that went postponed or started between selection and lock could ride its stale lineup flag into delivery

mitigated.action: breakeven derivation re-created in the repo (scripts/audit/skip_breakeven_derivation.py) and re-run on the box; the recorded constant was kept

verified_recovered.how: the re-derivation reproduced the recorded breakeven within its recorded band; inputs fingerprinted in docs/audit/2026-07-10-skip-breakeven-derivation.json

residual.text: streak.json and the pick file remain a two-file non-atomic pair under a crash between update_streak and the terminal pick save (a restart can re-apply a result); deferred, healed by the 02:00 replay + contest anchoring

the cached-fallback safety net can still deliver a pick whose game went postponed when no replacement is eligible, and postponed_pick health ignores delivered picks (round-3 F1 deferred; round-2 accepted 'deeper postponed-commit hardening')

by design the T-35 final fallback, and (after ea73b78 L1) a gate-only block at the in-loop fallback deadline, still deliver a projected double-down; manual bts run / bts orchestrate delivery bypasses both lineup gates (won't-fix L4, operator-gated recovery tools)
residual.source: 9643d83 body; ea73b78 body (L1, won't-fix L4); audit memo 'Won't-fix, recorded'

residual.text: the realized_calibration regime fingerprint (policy_npz_sha256, feature_env_hash) does not change on predictor-code-only changes, and partial/missing stamps on the newest pick fall back to the wall-clock deploy filter
restart-churn detection is best-effort: an unreadable systemctl skips the churn check quietly, leaving heartbeat freshness as the only liveness signal
verify-manifest checks referenced R2 objects for existence + size only; content hashes are verified only at restore
health lookback windows span 31 calendar days (pre-existing off-by-one, deferred as cosmetic)
the 0.744 breakeven is one model era's number: skip-shadow records carry the regime fingerprint but stratification is deferred, and the high-streak tail band runs above the headline value
public-mode reply dedup deferred (dormant while delivery is DM or private); static-capture bytes telemetry undercounts on a kill mid-capture
static-snapshot retention policy deferred; the pre-gzip plain-JSON backlog was left in place (F14)

watchdog.trigger: a cron job outside the scheduler samples bts-scheduler NRestarts every 5 min; +3 restarts within 20 or 60 min (+4 within 180 min), or a game day with no executed lineup check by the earliest game's first pitch minus 5 min, alerts even while the heartbeat is fresh (per-part boundaries for a split are in notes)
watchdog.recovery_assertion: NRestarts stays flat for at least 60 min, scheduler_state.json parses with no new *.corrupt-* quarantine, and the day records an executed lineup check followed by a scoreable commit or a deliberate skip
